q: MUDRA Bank initially functioned as a subsidiary of which institution?
explain: MUDRA began as a non-banking financial company and a subsidiary of the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI). It was later made a separate company.

q: Which scheme provides collateral-free loans to small and micro business enterprises and individuals in the non-agricultural sector?
explain: PMMY is the scheme under which MUDRA works: collateral-free loans for non-farm micro and small units. PMJDY is for bank accounts, PMSBY for accident insurance and PM-KISAN for farmer income support.

q: Which of the following institutions cannot grant loans under the MUDRA Yojana?
explain: Commercial banks, NBFCs and MFIs lend under PMMY. Payments banks are not permitted to lend, so they cannot grant MUDRA loans.

q: Which of the following statements about MUDRA Yojana is correct?
options: It has three products, Shishu, Kishor and Tarun, which show the stage of growth and funding need of the micro unit
MUDRA was set up in April 2016 as a wholly owned subsidiary of NABARD
Beneficiaries can get loans only above ₹5 lakh up to ₹50 lakh
Its loans are meant mainly for agricultural crop production
explain: The three-tier structure (Shishu, Kishor, Tarun) mirrors a business's growth stage. MUDRA was launched in April 2015, was initially linked to SIDBI, and PMMY loans go up to ₹10 lakh for non-farm units.

q: What is the maximum loan limit under the Kishor category of MUDRA Yojana?
explain: Kishor loans go up to ₹5 lakh. ₹50,000 is the Shishu ceiling and ₹10 lakh is the Tarun ceiling.

q: What is the size of the Credit Guarantee Fund created for MUDRA loans (as per the 2024-25 syllabus)?
explain: The Credit Guarantee Fund is ₹30 billion, which equals ₹3,000 crore. It reduces the credit risk of lenders financing micro units.

q: Loans in the Kishor category of MUDRA Yojana start above which amount?
explain: Shishu covers loans up to ₹50,000, so Kishor begins just above ₹50,000 and runs up to ₹5 lakh.

q: What was the initial capital of MUDRA Bank?
explain: MUDRA started with ₹200 billion (₹20,000 crore) of capital. The credit guarantee fund is a separate ₹30 billion (₹3,000 crore).

q: What is the maximum loan limit under the Shishu category of MUDRA Yojana?
explain: Shishu, the category for units just starting out, has a ceiling of ₹50,000.

q: What is the maximum loan available under the Tarun category of PMMY?
explain: Tarun is the highest tier, covering loans above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹10 lakh.

q: What is the full form of MUDRA?
options: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency
Micro Units Deposit and Reserve Agency
Medium Units Development and Refinance Agency
Micro Unit Development and Re-lending Association
explain: MUDRA stands for Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency. It focuses on micro enterprises and on refinance, not deposits.

q: On which date was MUDRA formally launched?
explain: MUDRA was formally launched on 8 April 2015. The day before, 7 April 2015, it was registered with the RBI as a Non-Banking Finance Institution.

q: Under which law was MUDRA registered as a company in March 2015?
explain: MUDRA was registered as a company under the Companies Act, 2013. Its NBFI registration was then obtained from the RBI on 7 April 2015.

q: About 5.77 crore small businesses were identified as MUDRA's target clients. Roughly what share of them were getting finance from regular banks?
explain: Only about 4% of these businesses had access to formal bank finance, which is why MUDRA aims to fund the unfunded through last-mile agents.

q: Out of the additional ₹1 trillion fund planned for PMMY, which category receives the largest share (40%)?
explain: The split is Shishu 40%, Kishor 35% and Tarun 25%, so the smallest loans get the biggest share.

q: What share of the additional PMMY fund of ₹1 trillion is allotted to the Kishor category?
explain: Kishor gets 35%. Shishu receives 40% and Tarun 25%, adding up to 100%.

q: Which of the following is NOT a loan category under PMMY?
explain: The three categories are Shishu, Kishor and Tarun. 'Yuva' is not a PMMY category.

q: What is a MUDRA Card?
options: A prepaid gift card for MUDRA staff
A debit card issued against the MUDRA loan account for the working-capital portion
A credit card that is issued only to NBFC officials
A forex card meant for exporters
explain: The MUDRA Card is a debit card linked to the loan account's working-capital (overdraft) portion, allowing multiple withdrawals and credits.

q: For how many years is a MUDRA Card valid?
explain: The card has a validity of 5 years, while the limit fixed on it is valid up to the due date of the overdraft limit.

q: How does MUDRA monitor lending under PMMY?
options: Through quarterly physical inspection by SIDBI staff
By collecting data only from RBI returns
Through a web portal that captures lending data in a granular way
explain: MUDRA was given the job of monitoring PMMY and set up a monitoring portal that records lending data in detail.

q: Which of the following borrowers falls within the kind of units MUDRA aims to refinance?
explain: MUDRA refinances loans to micro units such as small manufacturers, shopkeepers, fruit and vegetable vendors and artisans.

q: With which regulator was MUDRA registered as a Non-Banking Finance Institution on 7 April 2015?
explain: NBFC registration is done by the Reserve Bank of India, and MUDRA was registered with the RBI on 7 April 2015.

q: In which Union Budget was the formation of MUDRA first announced?
explain: The setting up of the agency was announced in the Union Budget for FY 2015-16, presented in February 2015.

q: Which statement best describes MUDRA's role?
options: It refinances banks, NBFCs and MFIs that lend to micro enterprises
It accepts savings deposits from individual small traders
It supervises all commercial banks on behalf of the RBI
It issues insurance policies to small shopkeepers
explain: MUDRA is a refinance agency: it supports lending institutions with low-cost funds rather than dealing directly with the public or acting as supervisor.
